words.gloss: even if they fail to harm

literal: To those who possess envy, that itself is sufficient; even if enemies fail to harm, it will yield ruin.
translation: For those who harbor envy, that vice alone is sufficient to destroy them; even if their enemies fail to do them harm, envy itself will yield their ruin.
modern: பொறாமை உடையவர்களுக்கு அந்தப் பொறாமை ஒன்றே போதுமானது; பகைவர்கள் தீங்கு செய்யத் தவறினாலும், அதுவே அவர்களுக்கு அழிவைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the self-destructive power of envy. For a person who possesses envy (அழுக்காறு உடையார்), no external enemies are required to bring about their downfall. Even if their enemies fail (வழுக்காயும்) to inflict harm, the envy itself is entirely sufficient (சாலும்) to yield (ஈன்பது) complete ruin (கேடு). The poet emphasizes that envy acts as an internal foe, making external adversaries redundant in causing one's destruction.
